findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot paginate datetime fields
findings.body: OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint uses OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by="-datetime", so self.key is "datetime" and get_item_key is called with a datetime.datetime object. This method does math.floor/ceil on that datetime, which raises TypeError as soon as a non-empty page needs next/prev cursor values. Additionally, value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor int instead of converting it to a UTC datetime for the SQL cursor comparison, so even if get_item_key were fixed, resumed pages would compare a datetime column with an integer. Consequence: optimized_pagination=true requests against audit logs with any results fail with a server error or produce invalid cursor queries.

findings.title: Eviction can silently drop the root span from a buffered segment
findings.body: The new size cap calls zpopmin on the whole sorted set to remove spans with the smallest end_timestamp_precise. The script does not know which member is the root span and has no guard against removing it. If the root span has the oldest timestamp, it gets evicted while the has-root-span flag remains set. The segment then flushes on the root-span timeout but contains no span whose span_id matches the segment key, so downstream receives a segment without its root/segment span and incomplete trace data.

findings.title: zunionstore sums duplicate span scores and corrupts eviction order
findings.body: Redis zunionstore defaults to SUM aggregation, unlike the previous set union which deduplicated members. If the same span payload is present in both source keys (possible with redelivery or reprocessing), its score becomes the sum of the two end_timestamp_precise values instead of the timestamp itself. Since eviction at line 63 uses zpopmin on these scores, duplicate spans can appear artificially new, causing the wrong spans to be evicted and making the 1000-span cap operate on incorrect ordering. Use MAX aggregation or otherwise deduplicate before union.

findings.title: Advanced negative-offset branch slices a QuerySet with a negative start
findings.body: When enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset < 0, start_offset is set to the negative cursor.offset and then queryset[start_offset:stop] is evaluated. Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative start offsets and emits an invalid negative OFFSET or raises, so the advertised advanced reverse pagination path cannot work. A crafted cursor with a negative offset on an endpoint using optimized_pagination=true can therefore cause a server error.
